It is asserted that utilization of a ring approach would simplify the task of delineating terminal areas, while achieving essentially the same result. From an environmental standpoint, the approach will result in the same impacts as the contour approach, assuming that approximately the same quantum of population and commercial activity would be captured.
5. Different Formula for Cities Having Physical Limitations From a demographic standpoint, it is apparent that the physical
characteristics of a city may influence the nature and extent of its
growth outward. Certain cities are bounded by natural physical barriers; such as oceans, lakes, or deserts, which can prevent diffusion
from occurring concentrically. It is, therefore, argued that the
same formula which is applied to cities such as Dallas or Atlanta
(having no physical limitations) should not be applied to cities such
as San Francisco or Cleveland (which can have up to 50 percent less
land area available for diffusion).
A.D. Little recommends that, in order to compensate for this lack of available land to develop, the formula for cities having physical limitations should be increased by 50 percent.
